item.description: With sales up 12%, pickles are moving beyond traditional role as a side to become an ingredient in their own right The humble pickled onion, long associated with classic pub culture, the ploughman’s lunch and cold festive buffets, is enjoying a revival as Britain’s appetite for pickles grows. item.title: 9/11 grounded US flights, but strangers moved a liver 800 miles to save a baby
item.description: In 2001, six-month-old Kareena needed a liver transplant and was too sick to leave hospital. When US flights were grounded after 9/11, strangers and Tennessee National Guard members moved the donor liver nearly 800 miles from Nashville to Houston. Twenty-five years later, Kareena has graduated from college and is studying health policy in law school. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Beijing tightens drone crackdown, bans possession, storage across city from Nov 15
item.description: As of November 15, Beijing will officially prohibit residents and businesses from owning drones. Existing drone owners must either sell their devices or dispose of them before the deadline. Infringers will face potential confiscation of their drones along with hefty fines. This regulation enhances security measures, significantly restricting drone operations within the city, following previous limitations on unauthorized flights and the classification of all airspace as restricted. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: S Korea's revised espionage law: How it affects countries beyond North Korea
item.description: South Korea's expanded espionage law now covers all foreign countries, not just North Korea. This revised Criminal Act carries a minimum three-year prison sentence for espionage offenses. The amendment addresses concerns about technology and industrial espionage involving non-North Korean actors. High-profile technology leak cases, including those involving Chinese firms, preceded this change. South Korea aims to strengthen its ability to prevent leaks of strategic technologies. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Young dieters in China are increasingly turning away from low-calorie foods in favour of a new trend: chewy snacks. item.title: In 2024, New York turned 250 Christmas trees into breakwaters to restore salt marsh
item.description: Discarded Christmas trees found a new purpose in Jamaica Bay, where they transformed into natural breakwaters at a wildlife refuge. The structures served to safeguard newly planted salt marsh vegetation from erosive waves. By the fall, these barriers effectively trapped sediment, partially burying themselves in the marsh. This innovative ecological restoration project showcased how recycled trees could enhance a living shoreline system, bolstering the marsh's resilience and self-protection. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: 25 years after 9/11, Ten House has just one active member left from that day
item.description: Sal Argano, the last firefighter from 2001 at FDNY’s Ten House, serves as a living link. He survived the September 11 attacks due to a temporary assignment elsewhere that morning. His firehouse, located across from the World Trade Center, was damaged and lost six members. Argano continues working to share firsthand accounts with younger generations and visitors. He remains at the station to preserve memories as others retire. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
